result.title: Efficient Multimodal Agents for Auditing 3D Worlds
result.summary: Multimodal agents can now build interactive 3D worlds and games, yet these worlds, like those built by people, often contain glitches such as floating objects, walls that can be walked through, or objects that change when no one is looking. An automatic auditor could check such worlds at scale and provide rewards for agents that build them, but only if it is both accurate and cheap. Auditing requires three abilities, namely navigating to the objects that may contain a glitch, triggering glitches that appear only after a specific behavior, and recognizing what is wrong. Current auditors are either accurate but slow and expensive or cheap but unreliable. We study how much of the audit small models can take on. A 4B vision language model fine-tuned end to end on verified trajectories of a frontier teacher guided by Bayesian search learns to navigate and trigger, and six such explorers together match a frontier model on both, but recognition stays far behind. We therefore build an auditor in which a swarm of small explorers navigates and triggers, and a frontier model reviews what they record and report. On WorldAuditBench, our auditor succeeds on 55.9% of 213 tasks in Unreal Engine 5 and Three.js worlds, 13.6 points above the strongest auditor reported, at less than a quarter of its cost. It matches the frontier reviewer exploring on its own at 4.6 times lower cost and about half the latency. Without further training, it also answers embodied questions about real-world scans, matching the frontier reviewer exploring on its own and surpassing four other frontier models by 6.4 to 16.6 points.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建 3D 世界自动审计系统：用在前沿教师轨迹上端到端微调的 4B VLM 群体担任探索者，负责导航与触发隐藏故障，再由前沿模型复核其记录并判定问题，在 WorldAuditBench 上以更低成本超过已有审计器。
AI.relevance_reason: 「小模型主动获取视觉证据、前沿模型做判定」的分工与 THINK/LOOK/STOP 中的证据获取、停止决策和成本分配有具体联系，可供核查哪些子能力可下沉到小模型、以及识别环节为何明显落后。
